clue.text: " Some beauty lies, the of neighbouring eyes " (Milton)

definitions.text: Some beauty lies, the of neighbouring eyes

parts.words: Some beauty lies, the of neighbouring eyes
parts.note: a line from Milton's poem L'Allegro with one word left out; the missing word names the beauty at whom every nearby eye gazes

explanation.surface: A quotation from Milton about a beauty who draws every eye nearby, with a gap for the solver to fill.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a fill-in-the-gap quotation: Milton's L'Allegro reads 'Where perhaps some beauty lies, / The cynosure of neighbouring eyes'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word Milton used means a centre of attention, something everyone looks towards, like the Pole Star guiding sailors.

clue.text: An element good with a motor

parts.note: a motor is a car
bon is French for good

explanation.surface: Someone praises a decent component of their car.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a chemical element, the basis of organic chemistry, with atomic number six.

clue.text: The Colonel of the Huts

parts.note: the clue points to the army officer whose surname was given to a design of curved corrugated-iron shed

explanation.surface: A military man is identified by the huts he is known for.
explanation.walkthrough: Lieutenant-Colonel Peter Nissen designed the half-cylinder corrugated-iron hut used by the British army in both world wars.
explanation.definitionFit: The hut takes its name from its inventor, an army colonel, so his surname is the word for the huts.

clue.text: A small coin makes a communist embittered

parts.note: a sou was an old French coin of little value
a red is a communist, from the red flag

explanation.surface: A trifling coin of money turns a communist sour about capitalism.
explanation.definitionFit: Soured describes someone made bitter, a close synonym of embittered.

clue.text: Created -a disturbance like Adam and Eve

definitions.meaning: to raise Cain is an idiom for making an uproar or causing trouble
in Genesis Adam and Eve brought up their son Cain, so they literally reared him

explanation.surface: The first couple in Eden caused a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for kicking up a fuss is read literally: Adam and Eve raised (brought up) their son Cain.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means making a fuss or row, and the first parents in Genesis also reared their son of that name.

clue.text: Appropriate mascot for the Met Office?

definitions.text: Appropriate mascot for the Met Office?

parts.words: Appropriate mascot for the Met Office
parts.note: the Met Office is Britain's weather forecaster; a castrated ram has a name that sounds like what they forecast

explanation.surface: Someone suggests a fitting emblem for the national weather service.
explanation.walkthrough: The Met Office is the UK's national weather service; the castrated male sheep it would adopt shares its sound with the weather it forecasts.
explanation.definitionFit: A wether is a castrated ram, an animal mascot whose name sounds like the forecasters' subject.

clue.text: Alienate the odd sergeant

indicators.note: odd signals that the letters of the following word are to be rearranged into something strange

explanation.surface: A peculiar sergeant puts everyone off him.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange someone is to make them hostile or distant, which is to alienate them.

clue.text: To offer one international status is a disadvantage

parts.note: to hand something over is to offer it
the Roman numeral I is one
a cap is awarded to a player chosen for their national side

explanation.surface: Being given a place in the national team turns out to be a burden.
explanation.definitionFit: A handicap is a hindrance or burden placed on someone, which is a disadvantage.

clue.text: Makes good provision among the Sappers

parts.note: the Royal Engineers, nicknamed the Sappers, are abbreviated RE
stores are provisions or supplies

explanation.surface: Army engineers are seen to supply their comrades properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' sits between the pieces as a link: provisions placed with the Sappers.
explanation.definitionFit: To make good damage is to repair it, which is what restoring does.

clue.text: Gunners given first knock by a Russian

parts.note: the Royal Artillery, the Gunners, are abbreviated RA
's put in, that is 'is put in': in cricket a side put in is sent to bat first, getting the first knock

explanation.surface: Artillerymen get the first innings in a cricket match against a Russian side.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Gunners given first knock' as RA'S PUT IN, the Gunners is put in to bat. In cricket a knock is an innings. Rasputin was the mystic at the last Tsar's court.
explanation.definitionFit: Grigori Rasputin was a Russian peasant mystic famous at the court of Nicholas II.

clue.text: Makes up for one in the Women's Service

indicators.note: in means the word for one is placed inside the abbreviation for the women's service

parts.note: the ATS, the Auxiliary Territorial Service, was the British army's women's branch in the Second World War
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman makes amends for a colleague serving in the women's army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: To atone is to make amends, to make up for a wrong.

clue.text: No writer looked astonished

parts.note: the letter O, a zero, stands for no or nothing
a pen is something that writes
eyed means looked at

explanation.surface: Someone with nothing to write with stared in amazement.
explanation.definitionFit: Being open-eyed is staring wide in surprise, so it means astonished.

clue.text: Australian town provides a card game

definitions.meaning: A town in northern New South Wales
..., also spelt cassino, is a card game in which players capture cards from the table

explanation.surface: A town in Australia offers a game of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a New South Wales town and a fishing-style card game for two to four players.

clue.text: Long hidden as an old sailer

indicators.note: old suggests the words have been worn out and reworked, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something old was concealed for a long time, like a ship of yore.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal is weak: 'old' marks the rearrangement of LONG HIDDEN, and 'as an' links to the definition. The Golden Hind was Francis Drake's ship on his round-the-world voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: Drake's galleon was a sailing ship, and a sailer is any vessel that goes under sail.

clue.text: Darling deed gets formal pardon

definitions.meaning: Grace Darling was the lighthouse keeper's daughter who rowed out to rescue shipwreck survivors in 1838
an official pardon granted as a favour

explanation.surface: A lovely deed earns someone an official pardon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Darling' looks like an endearment but is Grace Darling, an English heroine famed for a sea rescue in 1838.
explanation.definitionFit: An act of grace is a privilege or amnesty given as a favour, and Grace Darling's rescue was her act.

clue.text: Celebrity allows for lesser lights

parts.note: a star is a celebrity
lets means allows

explanation.surface: A famous name makes room for less famous performers.
explanation.definitionFit: Starlets are young actresses who have yet to become big names, so they are minor figures.

clue.text: When the answer for the footballer may well be a lemon

definitions.text: When the answer for the footballer may well be a lemon

parts.words: When the answer for the footballer may well be a lemon
parts.note: players traditionally sucked slices of lemon at the interval of a match

explanation.surface: A footballer is told he is a lemon, a dud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lemon' suggests a failure, but footballers were traditionally given lemon slices to suck during the interval.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the break between the two halves of a football match, when lemons were served.

clue.text: Write a label on the War Dept.

parts.note: to pen is to write
a tag is a label

explanation.surface: Someone is told to write a label on a government department's file.
explanation.definitionFit: The five-sided building in Virginia houses the US Department of Defense, formerly the War Department.

clue.text: The steady blows of commerce

parts.note: blows is read as winds blowing, and commerce suggests trade: steady tropical winds that carried merchant ships

explanation.surface: Commerce is pictured taking steady punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blows' looks like punches but means winds that blow; these steady winds were named for their use on trading voyages.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the constant easterly winds of the tropics, long relied on by merchant sailing ships.

clue.text: Colour sounds like a town in Oxfordshire

indicators.note: sounds like says the colour's name is pronounced the same as the town

parts.note: Bicester is a market town in Oxfordshire, pronounced 'bister'

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a paint shade shares its name with an English town.
explanation.walkthrough: Bicester, a town in the English county of Oxfordshire, is said 'bister', which is how the pigment name is pronounced.
explanation.definitionFit: Bistre is a brown pigment made from soot, used in pen-and-wash drawings.

clue.text: Pretty good for, a Scot

definitions.meaning: the word means attractive or comely
in Scots the word also means fine or good

explanation.surface: A Scot finds something pretty and good.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma after 'for' is a printing slip; read 'Pretty good, for a Scot'. The Scots word bonnie means pretty and also fine or good.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish word means attractive and also fine, so it fits both senses.

clue.text: Pious hero

parts.note: Virgil repeatedly calls the hero of the Aeneid 'pius', dutiful to gods and family

explanation.surface: A righteous champion.
explanation.walkthrough: Virgil's standing epithet for his Trojan hero is 'pius', loyal to gods, country and family.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trojan hero of Virgil's Aeneid is known by the epithet 'pius', dutiful.

clue.text: Those in charge of the game include it for repairs

indicators.note: include means the referees' word takes the next word inside it

parts.words: Those in charge of the game
parts.note: refs, short for referees, run a game

explanation.surface: Match officials add an item to a list for maintenance work.
explanation.definitionFit: Refits are overhauls or renovations, especially of ships, so they are repairs.

clue.text: One giant reform in Greek drama

indicators.note: reform tells us to form the letters again in a new order

explanation.surface: A giant reformed in a Greek play.
explanation.definitionFit: Antigone is the tragedy by Sophocles about Oedipus's daughter who buries her brother.

clue.text: Holly gives spirit to Ireland

parts.note: Erin is a poetic name for Ireland
go means energy or spirit

explanation.surface: A sprig of holly brings cheer to Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: Eringo, also spelt eryngo, is sea holly, a spiny coastal plant whose candied root was once eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: The eryngo is sea holly, a spiny plant with holly-like leaves.

clue.text: What one keeps to avoid familiarity

definitions.text: What one keeps to avoid familiarity

parts.words: What one keeps to avoid familiarity
parts.note: a reserved person stays aloof, keeping others at arm's length

explanation.surface: A guide to staying reserved with others.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'keep one's distance' means to stay aloof.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping your distance means staying aloof and not getting too friendly.

clue.text: Sounds severe for a novelist

indicators.note: sounds says the novelist's name is pronounced like the word for severe

parts.note: stern means severe

explanation.surface: Someone says a writer comes across as harsh.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Sterne was the eighteenth-century novelist who wrote Tristram Shandy.

clue.text: And eateth not the bread of " (O.T.)

definitions.text: And eateth not the bread of

parts.words: And eateth not the bread of
parts.note: the end of a verse from Proverbs praising the good wife, with its final word left out: she never eats the bread of sloth

explanation.surface: An Old Testament verse with its last word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Fill the gap: Proverbs 31:27 says the virtuous woman 'eateth not the bread of idleness'. O.T. is the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word means sloth or laziness, which the virtuous woman of Proverbs avoids.
